newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's SFC issues financial industry management code.
newsitem.headline: HK's SFC issues financial industry management code.

text.p: Hong Kong's financial industry watchdog on Thursday proposed management and corporate control guidelines aimed at preventing another fiasco like those in Barings futures trading or Sumitomo Corp copper trading.
"That is the Holy Grail of a regulator," said Anthony Neoh, chairman of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The SFC issued a consultation paper on management and internal control guidelines for firms in the financial industry, setting out a checklist of basic principles of good management for those in the financial industry.

"The need to ensure that the business structures and operations of financial professionals exist in an environment in which adequate internal controls are present has become abundantly clear due to the events of the past several years," said Neoh.

The guidelines, which will not have the force of law, will apply to all those registered with the SFC, including dealers, dealing partnerships, investment advisers, investment advisers' partnerships and licensed leveraged foreign exchange traders.
The guidelines are to be included in the commission's code of conduct, which was first issued in 1993.

The main objectives of the guidelines were to safeguard the assets of a firm and its clients; proper maintenance of thorough and reliable accounting and financial records and other information used by the business; and compliance by the firm with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, the commissioner said.

He added the SFC would adopt a pragmatic approach in evaluating the adequacy of a firm's internal control system by taking into account its particular circumstances, such as its size and capital base and its base of operations.
He said large firms would already be in compliance literally with the guidelines and some would exceed them.

Neoh said regulation of the financial industry in Hong Kong fell somewhere between those of Britain and the United States, in that the Hong Kong system sought to adhere both to the letter and the spirit of the law without seeking the detailed codification of U.S. regulation.

The proposed guidelines are divided into eight sections, each of which identifies a specific objective, followed by control guidelines: management and supervision; segregation of duties and functions, recruitment and training; information management; compliance; audit; operational controls and risk management.
The consultation period will run until January 31, 1997. The commission hoped to introduce the guidelines into its Code of Business Conduct by April 1997.
The commissioner also said that a revised Securities and Futures Bill should be issued in the coming week for a second period of consultation.
The bill, which was a complete review and updating of the regulatory framework of the financial industry, underwent a first period of consultation that was completed earlier this year.
